extracted.intended_audience: Marie Skłodowska-Curie (MSCA) Individual Fellowship holders (MSCA IF fellows) preparing their final report
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and an example public synopsis / final report for the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Individual Fellowship (H2020) final reporting process, including what to include in required sections and practical submission tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1 – Summary of the context and overall objectives of the project (including conclusions for the final period)
rubrics_metrics.description: This section should include information on: What is the problem/issue being addressed? Why is it important for society? What are the overall objectives? (For the final period, include the conclusions of the action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the problem/issue and societal importance, state overall objectives clearly, and for the final report include the conclusions of the action. The blog's public synopsis illustrates how to describe the project's aims (e.g., research questions about how engineering and architecture students learn; objectives such as developing and promoting better ways to teach STEM students; transforming engineering into a more diverse and creative field; and investigating how design projects influence cognitive and epistemological development). Use concise public-facing language suitable for the Participant Portal's public synopsis field.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2 – Work performed from the beginning of the project to the end of the period covered and main results achieved (including exploitation and dissemination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work performed via work packages (WPs); report main results achieved so far. (For the final period please include an overview of the results and their exploitation and dissemination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe activities and outputs per work package (e.g., qualitative studies, development of special-focus journal issues, training, public engagement). Include measurable outputs: conference publications, journal articles, encyclopedia entries, special issues edited, presentations delivered, public engagement activities, workshops for researchers/educators, training attended, supervision/mentoring, appointments (editorial roles), teaching qualifications, and funds/contracts secured. Explain dissemination and knowledge transfer activities and how results are being exploited (e.g., publications forthcoming, datasets to inform future papers, workshops, community up-skilling). Provide enough detail to show achievement beyond planned tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 – Progress beyond the state of the art; expected results until end of project; potential impacts (including socio-economic and wider societal implications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the action has pushed frontiers of the field, anticipated/expected results through to project end, and potential socio-economic and wider societal impacts to date and expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain contributions beyond current state-of-the-art (e.g., new understandings, models, tools). Describe concrete impacts already realized and those anticipated (e.g., influencing teaching practice, improving student retention, increasing diversity, raising focus on ethics/sustainability, production of tools/models for educators and industry, enhancing public perception). Include examples demonstrating wider reach (e.g., nomination for awards, community events, network leadership, masterclasses delivered). Link anticipated impacts to exploitation and dissemination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project public website address (URL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the address (URL) of the project's public website as requested by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add the public website URL that presents project outputs and information. If you do not have a separate project site, indicate whether you repurposed an existing blog/website. Make the site accessible for public visibility and link it in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images attached to the Summary for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach images to the Summary for publication as requested by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select images suitable for publication with the public summary (e.g., photos from project activities). Ensure images meet any Commission technical or content requirements (the blog notes the Commission requests images attached to the Summary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public synopsis submission constraints and template access (formatting/verbosity requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural constraints for the Participant Portal: the public synopsis text is limited to a specific character count (the author notes 7,480 characters) and the full report uses a required PDF template that must be located/downloaded via a specific button in the portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware the Participant Portal may not show length limits until after entering text; the public synopsis field has a strict character limit (author observed 7,480 characters). Locate and download the blank PDF template for the full final report from the portal (a specific button contains the template). Prepare concise public statements that fit the character limit and complete the full report using the provided template. The blog emphasizes that these portal quirks can be surprising, so plan ahead (draft offline, count characters, and find template button).
